intervals.note: Start is the commissioning of ACT, the earliest sourced instrument in the area that the later literature places in the Parque Astronómico Atacama (ACT DR6 maps paper: "ACT was a 6-meter off-axis Gregorian telescope, located at 5190 meters altitude in the Parque Astronómico Atacama"). The park itself received its formal concession only in 2014 (next row); CONICYT states that two projects were already operating in the area at that time.

name: Parque Astronómico Atacama
notes: No website for the park itself is recorded: no park site was fetched. CONICYT's astronomy news page is cited for the opening and the concession.

Sourced site names differ by experiment (ACT: "slopes of Cerro Toco"; POLARBEAR: "James Ax Observatory ... on Cerro Toco"; CLASS: "Cerro Toco"; Simons Observatory: "near the summit of Cerro Toco"); all four are on Cerro Toco within about a kilometre of each other and all four papers/pages place them in the Parque Astronómico Atacama. See the four site records.

operator.note: The 2014 concession was presented to the president of CONICYT. Later papers (ACT DR6 maps, 2025) cite the Agencia Nacional de Investigación y Desarrollo (ANID) as the agency under whose auspices ACT operated in the park; the CONICYT-to-ANID succession is not stated in any fetched source, so the 2014 holder is recorded.

summary.plain: A high-altitude desert park in northern Chile reserved for astronomy. Several microwave telescopes that map the afterglow of the Big Bang stand on and near Cerro Toco inside it, including the Atacama Cosmology Telescope, the Simons Observatory, POLARBEAR/Simons Array and CLASS.
summary.technical: Astronomical park of about 36,000 ha on the Llano de Chajnantor (San Pedro de Atacama, Antofagasta Region), held by CONICYT under a 50-year territorial concession from January 2014. Hosts ground-based CMB experiments at ~5200 m on Cerro Toco: ACT (2007-2022), POLARBEAR/Simons Array, CLASS and the Simons Observatory; the baseline Chilean site of the proposed CMB-S4 (cancelled 2025).
